newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA SAYS NO PLAN TO CUT STATUTORY RESERVES.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA SAYS NO PLAN TO CUT STATUTORY RESERVES.

text.p: Malaysia has no immediate plan to cut banks' statutory reserve requirement (SRR), government sources said on Thursday.
Financial markets have in the last hour been talking about a possible one percent cut in the SRR to help improve liquidity in the banking system.
"The rumour is not true. There's no such plan," said a government official.
Rumours of a meeting between bankers and officials of the central Bank Negara Malaysia to discuss the SRR issue were also not true, said the sources.

A recent tightening of market liquidity following a massive intervention by the central bank in the foreign exchange market to defend the ringgit from speculative attack, had prompted speculation that the SRR would be trimmed from its current 13.5 percent level.
The SRR, deposits that banks keep interest-free with the central bank, has been raised by two percentage points since the beginning of 1996.
